title: Microsoft Purview: Data Security Triage Agent remediation reminders in Teams
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's documented preview behaviour. The opt-in default, licensing, Teams delivery controls and PowerShell command are supported; the briefing also preserves the documented caveat about app-availability propagation.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is December CY2027, presented as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability as a release phase.
claims.quote:
"releasePhase": [
    "General Availability",
    "Preview"
  ]

claims.claim: The roadmap also lists Preview as a release phase.
claims.quote:
"releasePhase": [
    "General Availability",
    "Preview"
  ]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Web is the only platform listed in the roadmap record.
The record does not list US Government clouds.
The roadmap describes visibility into remediation progress through the Data Security Posture Management dashboard.
claims.quote: Its’ closed-loop workflow ensures that remediation progress is tracked and confirmed, giving admins real-time visibility and control via the Data Security Posture Management dashboard.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview Data Security Triage Agent in DLP gains a sensitive-data remediation function through Teams.
claims.quote: The Data Security Triage Agent in Data Loss Prevention now offers a new sensitive data remediation function

claims.claim: Remediation reminders apply to SharePoint and OneDrive alerts triaged as Needs attention.
claims.quote: For Sharepoint/OneDrive alerts triaged as Needs Attention, the agent sends a Microsoft Teams chat to the last modified user of the file

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The agent sends a Teams chat to the user who last modified the file, asking that user to remove sensitive information.
claims.quote: the agent sends a Microsoft Teams chat to the last modified user of the file, and ask them to remove the sensitive information found in the file related to the alert.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents remediation reminders as preview and warns that their design may change before general availability.
claims.quote: Remediation reminders for the Data Security Triage Agent are currently in **Preview**. Features and steps described in this article might change before general availability.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Reminders are sent once daily.
claims.quote: Reminders are sent once daily to the user who is last modifier of the file in context

claims.claim: A reminder combines up to 10 files when multiple files require remediation.
claims.quote: (combining up to 10 files if multiple files require remediation).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The remediation message includes the file name.
claims.quote: The remediation message includes the file name and a description of what sensitive information requires attention.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The remediation message describes the sensitive information requiring attention.
claims.quote: The remediation message includes the file name and a description of what sensitive information requires attention.

claims.claim: A file remediated by the user is removed from the next day's reminder.
claims.quote: Once the last person who modified, remediates the file, the file is removed from the remediation reminder for the next day.

claims.claim: No reminder is sent when no files remain for remediation.
claims.quote: If no files are found, no reminder is sent.

claims.claim: Enabling remediation reminders also enables the Teams bot for the tenant.
claims.quote: Enabling this setting also enables the bot in Microsoft Teams for the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The DLP Triage Agent alert queue displays alert-level remediation progress.
claims.quote: You can view remediation status at the alert level on the Triage Agent alert queue in the DLP solution.

claims.claim: A fully remediated alert means users remediated all implicated files.
claims.quote: This view lets a user see fully remediated alerts, meaning users remediated all files implicated in the alert.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: In progress indicates outreach has occurred but remediation is incomplete.
claims.quote: *In progress* means that the Agent reached out to the user, but the user didn't remediate all the files yet.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Error indicates that the Teams message could not be sent.
claims.quote: *Error* indicates that the Teams message couldn't be sent.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Each alert's Related assets section shows individual file remediation status.
claims.quote: You can see the status inside each DLP alert in the *Related assets* section that lists all the files implicated in the alert and the respective remediation status.

claims.claim: The cited Learn setup page does not describe the roadmap's DSPM remediation-progress view.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Posture Management remediation Teams Triage. Read the complete cited DLP agent setup page, including both remediation-progress views; it describes the DLP alert queue and Related assets, not a DSPM dashboard view.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Remediation is admin-opt-in, with reminders off in the one-click setup and no reminders until enabled.
claims.quote:
The default settings for 'One-Click' setup are:

- Identity: Create and use agent identity
- Trigger: Run automatically based on a set schedule
- Alert timeframe: Triage alerts from the last 30 days
- Remediation reminder: Turned OFF (Preview)

claims.claim: Configuring the Teams settings requires Teams admin permissions.
claims.quote: You must have [Teams admin permissions](/en-us/microsoftteams/using-admin-roles) to configure the Microsoft Teams Admin Center settings described in this article.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[3].note
claims.claim: Delivery requires both org-wide Microsoft apps to be enabled and the agent's Teams app to be available.
claims.quote: Two settings must be correctly configured for the Data Security Triage Agent to send remediation messages through Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Purview automatically installs the Teams app for a user when sending that user's remediation message.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview automatically installs the app for a specific user at the time a remediation message is sent.

claims.claim: The app need not be preinstalled; it must be available rather than blocked.
claims.quote: The Data Security Triage Agent app doesn't need to be preinstalled for users. Microsoft Purview automatically installs the app for a specific user at the time a remediation message is sent. The app only needs to be *available* (not blocked) in your organization.

claims.claim: Remediation-enabled policies are always a subset of triage-enabled policies.
claims.quote: Policies enabled for remediation are always a subset of policies enabled for triage.

claims.claim: The agent can be assigned its own Agent Identity.
claims.quote: An agent now has its own agent identity

claims.claim: Alternatively, the agent can use the identity of the user setting it up.
claims.quote: or can be set up by assigning the user's identity who is setting the agent.

claims.claim: Agent Identity allows the agent to access data and take actions.
claims.quote: The agent is assigned **Agent Identity**, which allows it to access data and take actions

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The triage agent supports only alerts from policies in active mode.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP only supports alerts from policies that are in active mode.

claims.claim: The agent does not triage alerts from policies running in simulation mode.
claims.quote: It doesn't triage alerts from DLP policies that are running in simulation mode.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed: the setup page requires both standard per-seat licensing and pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: This agent requires [both the standard per seat licensing model and the pay-as-you-go billing model](purview-billing-models).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The organisation must be licensed for Microsoft Data Loss Prevention to use the DLP triage agent.
claims.quote:
Your organization must be licensed for:

- Microsoft Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to use the DLP triage agent.

claims.where: front matter: cost; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cost is variable because the agent consumes Security Copilot security compute units as it performs its tasks.
claims.quote: The agent consumes security compute units (SCUs) as it performs its tasks.

claims.claim: The setup page requires SCUs to be provisioned for the triage agent to work.
claims.quote: You must have SCUs provisioned for the triage agent to work.

claims.claim: SCU consumption depends on the number and type of alerts processed.
claims.quote: The number of SCUs consumed depends on the number and type of alerts that are processed.

claims.claim: The preview remediation capability costs nothing extra beyond the SCUs needed to triage the alert first.
claims.quote: The Remediation Capability doesn't cost anything extra. The only costs associated with using this capability are the SCUs needed to triage the DLP alert first.

claims.claim: The triage agent's underlying SCU consumption is metered independently of enabling remediation.
claims.quote: The agent consumes security compute units (SCUs) as it performs its tasks.

claims.claim: Provisioned Security Copilot capacity is billed by the hour.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.claim: Overage capacity is billed on usage.
claims.quote: Provisioned capacity is billed by the hour while the overage capacity is billed on usage.

claims.claim: Overage units can be configured as unlimited or with a maximum amount.
claims.quote: Overage units are billed on-demand and can be set as unlimited or a maximum amount.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The capacity page documents automatically created inclusion capacity when Security Copilot inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7.
claims.quote: **Default Security Copilot Capacity** is the automatically created inclusion capacity that appears in your tenant when Security Copilot inclusion is enabled through Microsoft 365 E5 and E7.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to Security Copilot pricing pages for SCU pricing.
claims.quote: For more information, see [Microsoft Security Copilot pricing](https://aka.ms/CopilotforSecurity_Pricing) and the [Pricing calculator](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/calculator/?service=microsoft-copilot-for-security) page.

claims.claim: The tenant must be onboarded to Microsoft Security Copilot.
claims.quote: Your tenant must be onboarded to Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 data sharing must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable Microsoft 365 data sharing in Security Copilot.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview plug-in must be enabled in Security Copilot.
claims.quote: You must enable the Microsoft Purview plug-in in Microsoft Security Copilot.

claims.claim: A tenant can have only one instance of each agent.
claims.quote: There can be only one instance of each agent in a tenant, regardless of the portal in which it was deployed.

claims.claim: The agent can be deployed from either Microsoft Purview or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals

claims.claim: The agent can be managed and edited only from the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: The Triage Agent can be deployed from both Microsoft Purview and Defender XDR portals, but can only be managed, edited, and disabled from the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Deactivation is available only in the Microsoft Purview portal, including for agents deployed from Defender XDR.
claims.quote: Agent can only be deactivated from the Microsoft Purview portal even if it was deployed from the Defender XDR portal.

claims.claim: Deactivating the agent stops it from triaging alerts.
claims.quote: Deactivating the agent stops the agent from triaging alerts.

claims.claim: Deactivation does not remove the agent.
claims.quote: It doesn't remove the agent and it doesn't reset the **Select alert timeframe** reference point in time.

claims.claim: The feature's Teams page says setting app availability to No one immediately stops all remediation messages, with the briefing separately reporting the general propagation caveat.
claims.quote: This result is a failsafe mechanism--if you need to *immediately* stop all remediation messages, set availability to **No one**.

claims.claim: Blocking the app is a hard block on delivery to the blocked user even if a remediation message has been generated.
claims.quote: Blocking the app for a user is a hard block. Even if an alert is triaged and a remediation message is generated, the message *won't* be sent to users for whom the app is blocked.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Policy scoping determines which files trigger reminders; policies not enabled for remediation do not generate those messages.
claims.quote: This approach limits remediation by controlling which DLP policies trigger remediation messages. Users who violate policies that aren't enabled for remediation don't receive Teams messages from the agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends policy scoping for routine control and Teams blocking as an additional safeguard.
claims.quote: Use policy scoping in Purview for routine control over what files and locations trigger remediation. Use Teams Admin Center blocking as another safeguard

claims.claim: Microsoft identifies org-wide Microsoft apps being enabled while the agent is individually blocked as a common misconfiguration.
claims.quote: A common misconfiguration occurs when the org-wide Microsoft apps toggle is *enabled* but the Data Security Triage Agent app is *individually blocked*.

claims.claim: General Teams guidance says UI or PowerShell availability changes can take up to 24 hours to apply to all users.
claims.quote: UI or PowerShell changes take up to 24 hours to apply to all users, consistent with anytime UI or PowerShell updates occur, not just immediately after migration completion.

claims.claim: Remediation reminders are under Microsoft Purview portal > Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration > Remediation reminders in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: Select **Agent configuration** for editing and configuring settings like Trigger, alert timeframe, remediation reminders, reminder duration, and policy scope.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for setting remediation reminders or reminder duration.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Data Security Triage Agent remediation reminders policy scope API PowerShell configuration; Data Security Triage Agent remediation API. Read the setup and Teams configuration pages; results document UI settings, not an automation operation.

claims.claim: Remediation policy scope is under Purview > Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > Edit agent > Agent configuration > Set agent scope > Edit > Select policies > Remediation.
claims.quote:
Under **Set agent scope**, select **Edit**.
5. In the **Select policies** panel, enable the **Remediation** toggle only for the policies where you want remediation messages sent to users.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for remediation policy scope.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Data Security Triage Agent remediation reminders policy scope API PowerShell configuration; Data Security Triage Agent remediation API. Read the setup and Teams configuration pages; the scope procedure is UI-only and no relevant operation was found.

claims.claim: App availability is under Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Data Security Triage Agent > Users and groups > Edit availability.
claims.quote:
Go to **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**.
3. Search for **Data Security Triage Agent** and select it.
4. Go to the **Users and groups** tab.
5. Select **Edit availability**.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone to set app availability to Everyone.
claims.quote: PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone

claims.claim: Everyone makes the app available to everyone in the organisation.
claims.quote: | `Everyone` | Available to all org users, new users, and guests.

claims.claim: The command's Id parameter identifies the Microsoft Teams application.
claims.quote:
### -Id

Application ID of Microsoft Teams app.

claims.claim: The Microsoft apps toggle is under Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps.
claims.quote:
Go to **Teams apps** > **Manage apps**.
3. Select **Actions** > **Org-wide app settings**.
4. In the **Org-wide app settings** panel, set the **Microsoft apps** toggle to **On**.

claims.claim: No automation operation was found for the org-wide Microsoft apps toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams org-wide app settings Microsoft apps toggle PowerShell API; Microsoft apps org-wide PowerShell. Read Teams configuration and app-centric management; returned cmdlet references concern Custom Apps, not this Microsoft apps toggle.

claims.claim: Deactivation is under Purview > Agents > Explore agents > Go to agent > ellipses (three dots) > Deactivate agent.
claims.quote:
Select **Go to agent** for the agent you want to deactivate.
5. On the far right upper right hand corner of the agent overview page, select the ellipses (three dots) that are located *next to* the **Edit agent** button.
6. Select **Deactivate agent**.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for deactivating this Purview DLP agent.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Data Security Triage Agent deactivate agent usage monitoring API PowerShell. Read the setup page's deactivation procedure; results show portal deactivation and no relevant API or PowerShell operation.

claims.claim: SCU monitoring is under Purview > Agents > Explore agents > View agent > Edit agent > Usage monitoring.
claims.quote:
select **Agents**.
3. Select **Explore agents**.
4. Select **View agent** for agent you want to edit.
5. Select **Edit agent**.
6. Select **Usage monitoring**.

claims.claim: No automation operation was found for monitoring this agent's SCU consumption.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Data Security Triage Agent deactivate agent usage monitoring API PowerShell; Security Copilot agent usage monitoring consumption API get usage Purview SCU. Read DLP setup and Security Copilot manage-usage; no corresponding automation operation found.

claims.claim: The agent's Usage monitoring entry reports consumption through Security Copilot's monitoring tool rather than itself imposing a spending limit.
claims.quote:
Select **Usage monitoring**.
7. You can track your SCU consumption in the [usage monitoring tool](/en-us/copilot/security/manage-usage).

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Reminder duration configures how many days the agent follows up about unremediated files.
claims.quote: The reminder duration reports the number of days the Agent should follow up with the user on files that aren't remediated.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can restrict recipients through the app's Specific users or groups availability setting.
claims.quote: Change the availability from **Everyone** to **Specific users or groups**, then add only the users or groups who should receive remediation messages.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: A Purview admin configuring the agent may lack the Teams admin permissions needed for the Teams settings.
claims.quote: The Purview admin or analyst who configures the triage agent might not have permissions to access the Microsoft Teams Admin Center.

claims.claim: The triage agent as a whole covers alerts from Exchange, Devices, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams.
claims.quote: The Triage agent in DLP triages alerts from Exchange, Devices, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams.
